top_evidence.document_title: Conversion hepatectomy and survival in initially unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma: a systematic review and meta-analysis with quantitative bias analysis
top_evidence.text: The protocol was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261382843). This systematic review was conducted in accordance with the Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions and reported according to the PRISMA 2020 statement [11,14]. The literature search was updated during manuscript revision without changes to the prespecified PICO framework. No substantive amendments to the registered protocol were made. The complete database-specific search strategies are provided in Additional file 1 (Table S1).

top_evidence.document_title: Conversion hepatectomy and survival in initially unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma: a systematic review and meta-analysis with quantitative bias analysis
top_evidence.text: The datasets supporting the conclusions of this article are included within the article and its additional files. Extracted study-level and endpoint-level data are provided in Additional file 1. Analysis code is available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request.

top_evidence.document_title: Conversion hepatectomy and survival in initially unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma: a systematic review and meta-analysis with quantitative bias analysis
top_evidence.text: Analyses were performed in R version 4.5.3 using prespecified analysis code. Random-effects meta-analysis, prediction intervals, leave-one-out analysis, influence diagnostics, and small-studyeffect tests were implemented with the metafor package [15]. E-value calculations, deterministic tipping-point QBA, probabilistic QBA, timing-bias scenario analyses, and funnel-plot diagnostics were applied to the extracted comparative HR dataset. Package versions, session information, extraction tables, and analysis code were archived to support reproducibility [21].

top_evidence.document_title: Conversion hepatectomy and survival in initially unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma: a systematic review and meta-analysis with quantitative bias analysis
top_evidence.text: Additional file: Supplementary methods, tables and figures. This file contains database-specific search strategies, study characteristics, extracted endpoint-level HRs, ROBINS-I-informed judgments, E-value analyses, QBA assumptions and outputs, sensitivity analyses, small-studyeffect and reporting-bias diagnostics (Table S15 and Figure S5), GRADE certainty assessment, a structured comparison with prior systematic reviews (Table S13), and key full-text reports that appeared potentially eligible but were excluded from quantitative synthesis (Table S14). PRISMA 2020 checklist: Completed PRISMA 2020 checklist with manuscript locations for each reporting item. Declarations Ethics approval and consent to participate This systematic review used data from published studies and did not involve new recruitment of human participants, human tissue, or individual patient-level data. top_evidence.document_title: Conversion hepatectomy and survival in initially unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma: a systematic review and meta-analysis with quantitative bias analysis
top_evidence.text: We assessed the certainty of the body of evidence for each synthesized outcome using an adapted GRADE framework. Certainty was judged separately for OS and PFS/EFS, considering study design, risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness, imprecision, publication bias, and potential upgrading factors. ROBINS-I-informed domain judgments were used to inform the risk-of-bias domain, while heterogeneity statistics, prediction intervals, endpoint definitions, time-origin variability, and QBA findings informed the remaining domains. Because all included estimates came from non-randomized comparisons in which hepatectomy was usually assigned after treatment initiation, the GRADE assessment was specifically adapted to evaluate the certainty of these comparative prognostic and therapeutic associations.

top_evidence.document_title: Conversion hepatectomy and survival in initially unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma: a systematic review and meta-analysis with quantitative bias analysis
top_evidence.text: Descriptive supplementary diagnostics described the influence of individual estimates and selected analytic assumptions. These analyses were interpreted descriptively and did not change the overall direction of the pooled estimates (Additional file 1: Tables S10A-S10B). In diagnostics restricted to adjusted or time-dependent estimates, heterogeneity was lower and pooled estimates remained below 1.0 (OS HR 0.21 [95% CI 0.13-0.34]; PFS/EFS HR 0.35 [95% CI 0.24-0.49]).

top_evidence.document_title: Conversion hepatectomy and survival in initially unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma: a systematic review and meta-analysis with quantitative bias analysis
top_evidence.text: Because individual patient-level time-to-surgery data were unavailable across studies, immortaltime bias could not be formally corrected using a unified time-dependent model [19,20]. We therefore performed an aggregate scenario analysis to examine how the pooled estimates would change under different assumptions about the time from treatment initiation to surgery and the median survival of the non-surgical comparator group. The calculation details are provided in Additional file.

top_evidence.section: Results > Study Selection And Included Studies
top_evidence.text: Fourteen comparative survival studies met the eligibility criteria and contributed 24 endpointspecific HRs comparing hepatectomy with non-hepatectomy management, including 14 OS estimates and 10 PFS/EFS estimates (Figure 1).
